newsitem.title: UK: Rowland hits out at Lonrho /JCI merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Rowland hits out at Lonrho /JCI merger talk.

text.p: British business tycoon Tiny Rowland on Friday hit out in full-page newspaper ads at the merger talks between South Africa's JCI Ltd and Lonrho Plc, the firm he left after a bitter row two years ago.

In big, bold print, the advertisements shouted "Lonrho-JCI merger: will two losers make one winner?," and were signed by Rowland. The ads were placed in widely-circulated broad sheets The Times and Daily Telegraph.
JCI and Lonrho, which Rowland led as chief executive for 32 years, last week announced they were discussing a tie-up. Such a merger would create one of the world's largest mining houses.
Negotiations continued this week, but Lonrho said talks were still in their early stages.
In the ads, Rowland said Lonrho has nothing to gain from the tie-up as it would narrow the UK' company's asset base while increasing risk in the longer term.
JCI -- taken over by Mzi Khumalo's African Mining Group earlier this year -- was described by Rowland as a "loser", which is still under the control of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd.
"JCI has not had a popular launch, and in addition the new board has many covenants over its decision making, imposed by Anglo as principal lender," Rowland said in his ad.
Rowland also lashed out at Lonrho which he has constantly criticised after being ousted from the board in March 1995.
"Our board cannot bring shareholder value to us," Rowland said.
Lonrho's shares, among the worst performers on the London Stock Exchange last year, were unchanged at 138-1/2 pence on Friday morning.
They had initially perked up to 144-1/2 pence after news broke of the JCI merger talk nearly two weeks ago. But shares began to retreat a couple of days later to ease back to current levels.
